html:
Viriathus was a leader of the Lusitanians, a people of the west of the Iberian Peninsula, who fought the Roman Republic from about 147 BCE until his death in 139 BCE.

Roman writers say he was a shepherd who survived a Roman massacre of Lusitanians who had surrendered. He led a guerrilla war in the hills, beat several Roman armies and forced Rome to a treaty. Rome then bribed three of his own men to murder him in his sleep.

Rome went on to conquer the region, which became the province of Lusitania. In the 1500s and again under Salazar Viriathus was made a hero of Portugal, a symbol of resistance to foreign rule. Compare the Numantine War in Spain, fought at the same time against Rome.
sum: Viriathus was a leader of the Lusitanians, a people of the west of the Iberian Peninsula, who fought the Roman Republic from about 147 BCE until his death in 139 BCE.
